summaries.summary: The final analysis explores emotionally charged words across industries using Positive Emotion and Negative Emotion categories in the Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) dictionary BIBREF29.
For all users in each industry, frequencies of Positive Emotion and Negative Emotion words normalized by text length are measured, and Table TABREF20 presents industry rankings.
A per-gender breakdown finds statistically significantly correlated industry rankings of relative frequencies INLINEFORM0 of emotionally charged words for the two genders.

Despite substantial gender imbalances in each industry, no statistically significant correlation was found between gender dominance ratio and positive or negative emotional word usage in either gender.
The paper examined predicting a social media user's industry, introduced an annotated dataset of over 20,000 blog users, and achieved overall accuracy up to 0.534 versus 0.188.
User metadata was incorporated into classifiers; stacking improved prediction accuracy to 0.643 on the test dataset, while Real Estate and Religion exceeded 0.80 and Banking was harder.
A qualitative analysis provided insights into industry language through top-ranked words, word semantic similarities, and relative frequency of emotionally charged words.
This material was supported in part by the National Science Foundation (#1344257) and the John Templeton Foundation (#48503), whose views are not necessarily reflected.
